On 13 April 2004 the Mayor of Sandanski advised the organisers of the Ilinden rally that Ilinden could hold a rally between 10 a.m. and 12 noon on 18 April 2004.

On 12 September 2004 about eighty metres from the monument to Gotse Delchev, a group of some forty police officers stopped the participants in the Ilinden rally.

According to the applicants, on 12 September 2004 the participants in Ilinden's rally refused to comply with the police conditions and were not allowed to approach the monument to Gotse Delchev.

The Mayor of Blagoevgrad banned Ilinden's rally planned for 12 September 2005, because it coincided with a children's celebration marking the opening of the school year.

On 12 September 2005 the Blagoevgrad police, relying on section 62 of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, ordered another of Ilinden's leaders not to organise or take part in rallies involving the laying of wreaths and flowers in front of Gotse Delchev's monument.

On 12 September 2005 approximately thirty uniformed and plain-clothes police officers surrounded the Ilinden members and supporters gathered in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad, blocked their way, seized the flags and placards they were carrying, and destroyed a wreath.

At about 12 noon on 23 April 2006 the police interrupted the Ilinden gathering, telling the participants that the time allowed by the Mayor of Sandanski had expired and they should disperse.

On 4 May 2006 the police prevented the participants in the Ilinden rally from moving towards Macedonia Square.

On 4 May 2006 the police, relying on section 55 of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, ordered the Ilinden participants in writing to refrain from participating in assemblies without permission from the Mayor of Blagoevgrad.

On 4 May 2006 the police, relying on section 55 of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, ordered the Ilinden participants in writing not to use placards, banners and other visual materials featuring texts with anti-Bulgarian content.
On 30 August 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad replied that the event planned for 12 September 2006 could not proceed, as it might breach public order and infringe the rights of others.

On 12 September 2006 Ilinden sought permission from the Mayor of Sandanski to rent a municipal hall on 15 October 2006, to hold a founding meeting needed for the organisation's registration as a political party.

On 26 September 2006 the Mayor of Sandanski replied that Ilinden's request to rent the municipal hall on 15 October 2006 could not be accommodated, as on 15 and 16 October 2006 the hall was due to host an international wrestling tournament.
On 5 October 2006 the Mayor of Sandanski confirmed that the hall would be in use on the requested date and stated that no other venue of such a size existed.

On 26 March 2007 the Mayor of Sandanski informed Ilinden that the rally could take place between 11 a.m. and 12 noon, as the police did not have the means of protecting a longer event.

On 22 October 2007 the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad imposed administrative fines of 200 Bulgarian levs (102.26 euros) each on the second applicant and on a number of members of Ilinden for having taken part in a banned rally, in breach of a public-order regulation issued by the Blagoevgrad Municipal Council.

The second applicant and two other members of Ilinden were arrested and taken to a police station on 4 May 2009.

Section 12(1) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that where the time or the place of the meeting, or the itinerary of the march, would create a situation endangering public order or traffic safety, the President of the Executive Committee of the People's Council, or the mayor, respectively, shall propose their modification.

Section 12(2) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the President of the Executive Committee of the People's Council, or the mayor, shall be competent to prohibit the holding of a meeting, demonstration or march where reliable information exists that it aims at the violent overturning of constitutional public order or is directed against the territorial integrity of the country.

Section 12(2) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the President of the Executive Committee of the People's Council, or the mayor, shall be competent to prohibit the holding of a meeting, demonstration or march where reliable information exists that it would endanger public order in the local community.

Section 12(2) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the President of the Executive Committee of the People's Council, or the mayor, shall be competent to prohibit the holding of a meeting, demonstration or march where reliable information exists that it would breach the rights and freedoms of others.
Section 12(3) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the prohibition shall be imposed by a written reasoned act not later than twenty-four hours following the notification.
Under section 62(1) of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, the police could, if necessary for the performance of their duties, issue orders to individuals or organisations.

Section 55(1), (4) and (5) of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, which superseded section 62 of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act on 1 May 2006, has almost identical wording and is currently in force.

According to the applicants, on 19 December 2006 two men approached the three Ilinden members at the stall in Sandanski, one of whom was the head of the Petrich chapter of the political party Attack, who shouted insults at them.

According to the applicants, on 19 December 2006 the head of the Petrich chapter of the political party Attack threw the materials on the stall to the ground, hit one of the members of Ilinden in the face, and tore apart an Ilinden poster.

In a decision of 25 January 2007 the Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office refused to open a criminal investigation into the assault of 19 December 2006, as the acts alleged in the complaint did not constitute publicly prosecutable offences.

The Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office stated in its decision of 25 January 2007 that the bodily injuries suffered by the first Ilinden member were minor and therefore gave cause for a private prosecution only.

The Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office stated in its decision of 25 January 2007 that the destroyed property was not of great value, making its destruction a trivial occurrence which should not be criminally prosecuted.
The Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office stated in its decision of 25 January 2007 that the proffering of insults also gave cause for a private prosecution only.

On appeal by the three Ilinden members, on 5 February 2007 the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office upheld the Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office decision of 25 January 2007, fully endorsing its reasoning.
